findings.title: The minimum token schema does not capture arbitrary expiry fields
findings.body: `z.string().toString()` is evaluated as a literal property name, not a wildcard key, and the same applies to the optional property on line 10. Consequently, normal fields such as `expires_in` or `expiry_date` are not validated or retained by this `z.object` (which strips unrecognized properties); depending on the computed keys, responses may also fail parsing. With credential syncing enabled, token refreshes across the affected apps therefore fail or lose their expiry data.

findings.title: The SafeParse wrapper is saved as the Google credential key
findings.body: `parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns the result of `safeParse`, which has the shape `{ success, data }`, but this line stores that whole result as `credential.key` instead of its `.data`. After a token refresh, the next Google auth initialization parses this wrapper as a Google credential and fails, leaving the integration unusable.

findings.title: The new credential update references an unimported Prisma client
findings.body: This file does not import or otherwise declare `prisma`, but the newly added refresh code calls `prisma.credential.update`. TypeScript compilation fails with an unresolved `prisma` name, preventing the app-store package or application from building.

findings.title: Salesforce refresh bypasses the configured credential-sync endpoint
findings.body: This refresh path calls Salesforce directly instead of using `refreshOAuthTokens`. When credential syncing is configured, Salesforce still refreshes against Cal.com's Salesforce app rather than the self-hosted platform's source of truth, so the advertised sync behavior does not work for Salesforce.

findings.title: The Salesforce connection uses the pre-refresh access token
findings.body: The newly added code obtains and stores a refreshed token, but the connection is then constructed with `credentialKey.access_token`, which came from the original credential and was not updated with `accessTokenParsed.data`. When the original token is expired, Salesforce API calls therefore use the expired token despite the successful refresh.

findings.title: Bigin sends a credential row ID as the user ID
findings.body: The third argument to `refreshOAuthTokens` is used as `calcomUserId`, but this call passes `credentialId`, the ID of the credential row, rather than the owning user's ID. The sync endpoint will look up the wrong user (or fail to find one), so Bigin token refreshes cannot reliably retrieve the correct user's credentials.

findings.title: Webex rejects the documented minimal sync response
findings.body: The sync endpoint is documented to return only an access token and expiry date, but the response is passed on to `webexRefreshedTokenSchema` at line 88, which also requires `scope`, `token_type`, `refresh_token`, and `refresh_token_expires_in`. A response following the stated sync contract fails validation, so Webex refreshes fail and the integration cannot use synced credentials.

findings.title: The synced Teams token is immediately treated as expired
findings.body: The sync endpoint is expected to return an access token and expiry date, but the refresh handling later derives `expiry_date` solely from `expires_in` and overwrites it with `Date.now()` when `expires_in` is absent. The next `getToken` call sees that timestamp as expired and calls the sync endpoint again, causing repeated refresh requests and potentially rate-limiting the integration.

findings.title: Zoom sync uses a different slug from the stored app credential
findings.body: The refresh request identifies Zoom as `zoomvideo`, while Zoom credentials are stored with `appId: "zoom"` (as shown by the callback). The receiving sync endpoint uses `appSlug` to identify the app, so it cannot reliably match this request to the Zoom credential.

findings.title: Concurrent initial webhooks can create duplicate credentials
findings.body: The lookup at line 62 and the create here are separate, non-atomic operations. If two deliveries for the same user and app arrive before either creates its row, both observe no credential and insert one. This leaves duplicate credentials, after which consumers using `findFirst` may select an arbitrary copy.
